messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 R CMD Problems...
parts:
Don't use --binary to build the package, just do
R CMD build ggplot2
Also follow this by
R CMD check ggplot_VERSIONNUMBER.tar.gz

(note that --binary produces a *.tgz file, whereas you really want
a .tar.gz file (and I know these files are in a way the same, but .tgz
is the suffix for OS X binary files, whereas .tar.gz is for source
packages))

Also remember (this is important) to change the email address in the
Maintainer line in the ggplot2/DESCRIPTION file from Hadley's address
to your own. This email address is how winbuilder gets in touch with
you.

Kasper

parts:
Oh...I think I may finally have it.

Here is the process I came up with for downloading and producing a package of the development version for ggplot2:
(1) Using your favorite method, download latest development version of ggplot2 from github. For example, navigate to
http://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/tree/master,
select download, and choose either zip or tar.gz.

(2) Once the hadley-ggplot2-xxx.zip or hadley-ggplot2-xxx.tar.gz is downloaded, uncompress, and rename the uncompressed folder to just ggplot2. For example,
.../Documents/hadley-ggplot2-c18612033a01175fe1c4396b9d51ada6131e81e8.zip
after uncompressing it becomes
.../Documents/hadley-ggplot2-c18612033a01175fe1c4396b9d51ada6131e81e8
and then renaming it becomes
.../Documents/ggplot2

(3) Now, open the terminal and navigate to the folder where the uncompressed and renamed folder is stored, i.e. step accomplished in (2).
For example,
$ pwd
.../Documents
$ ls
ggplot2
...
$ R CMD build ggplot2


(4) Once in the terminal Window, type "R CMD build ggplot2" to build the ggplot2_0.8.3.tar.gz package, which can be used on a Windows machine via install.packages("ggplot2").

The results should be similar to the following:
$ R CMD build ggplot2
* checking for file 'ggplot2/DESCRIPTION' ... OK
* preparing 'ggplot2':
* checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... OK
* removing junk files
* checking for LF line-endings in source and make files
* checking for empty or unneeded directories
* building 'ggplot2_0.8.3.tar.gz'


I haven't had a chance to test out the resulting ggplot2_0.8.3.tar.gz on a Windows machine, but should be able to very soon be able to check that out.

Thank you again for all the help getting this far. I am really looking forward to using some of the development additions Hadley has been working on.

Take care.

Jason, you are not done yet. ggplot2_0.8.3.tar.gz is a source package,
ready for distribution. In order to use it on WIndows, you will need
to get it converted to a binary package, using winbuilder.

You need to do the following.
1) Edit the ggplot2/DESCRIPTION file in order to change the maintainer
email from Hadleys to your own.
2) Issue R CMD build and create a file ggplot2_0.8.3.tar.gz (but note
that this one has a changed email address)
3) Run
R CMD check ggplot_0.8.3.tar.gz
to make sure that 2) was succesful.
3) submit ggplot2_0.8.3.tar.gz to "winbuilder" using the instructions on
http://129.217.207.166/index.htm
(starting from bullet point 3) which will return you a file called
ggplot2_0.8.3.zip

That final file ggplot2_0.8.3.zip is ready for installation on Windows.

Kasper
